paper_diagnosis: Neutropenic enterocolitis during treatment of breast cancer
disease_label_per_paper: Neutropenic enterocolitis in a young patient with breast cancer after TAC chemotherapy
presentation_summary: A 22-year-old woman with breast cancer received docetaxel, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide with pegfilgrastim support.
On the seventh day after chemotherapy she presented to the oncology ward with fever, severe abdominal pain scored 8 on a VAS scale, and obstinate constipation.
She was neutropenic with neutrophils 500/mm3, and CT showed severe right-sided colonic and cecal wall thickening with mucosal hyperemia and submucosal hypodensity.
Despite medical therapy and neutrophil recovery, abdominal pain worsened and repeat CT showed progression, leading to right hemicolectomy.

actual_treatment.source_text_value: empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy (piperacillin/tazobactam and amikacin)
GCSF (filgrastim 30 one administration per day that was continued for 2 days until neutrophil count was >1,000/mm3)
hydration, bowel rest, and parenteral nutrition
right hemicolectomy with resection of the caecum and right and transverse colon till the splenic flexure with lateral ileostomy

outcome.source_text_value: The paper reports surgery and histology; it does not report death.
